questions.q: Why does this dashboard connect to dw.FactWorkOrder using Import instead of DirectQuery?
options: The warehouse is a nightly-refreshed batch target, not a live operational system, so there's no reason to pay DirectQuery's per-click query cost — and Import unlocks the full DAX surface the Scrap Rate measure needs
DirectQuery is not supported for SQL Server data sources at all
Import is required any time a report uses more than one visual
DirectQuery would delete the source warehouse tables after the first refresh
questions.explain: Import is the right fit for a batch-refreshed warehouse and gives the measure DIVIDE() needs; DirectQuery would add live-query overhead for no benefit here.

questions.q: What does the Scrap Rate measure, written as DIVIDE(SUM(FactWorkOrder[ScrappedQty]), SUM(FactWorkOrder[OrderQty])), return on a date with zero work orders?
options: Blank, because DIVIDE() returns blank instead of an error when the denominator is zero
An error, because dividing by zero always throws in DAX
Zero, because DIVIDE() always substitutes zero for a blank denominator
The prior date's scrap rate, carried forward automatically
questions.explain: DIVIDE() is used specifically because it returns blank instead of throwing a divide-by-zero error, which the raw / operator would do.

questions.q: Which two columns does the OnTimeFlag calculated column compare?
options: EndDateKey and DueDateKey
StartDateKey and EndDateKey
OrderQty and StockedQty
ProductKey and ScrapReasonKey
questions.explain: OnTimeFlag buckets each work order by comparing when it actually finished (EndDateKey) to when it was supposed to (DueDateKey).

questions.q: What does the production-volume-by-product visual read?
options: SUM(OrderQty) grouped by ProductName from DimProduct
COUNTROWS of DimScrapReason
AVERAGE(ScrappedQty) grouped by ScrapReasonName
MAX(DueDateKey) grouped by StartDateKey
questions.explain: Production volume by product sums OrderQty and groups it by the product name pulled in from DimProduct.

questions.q: Why is it significant that this dashboard reads dw.FactWorkOrder directly, rather than a separate extract or spreadsheet copy?
options: It means Power BI and the SSRS report from Lesson 7 share exactly the same source and logic, with nothing recalculated or restated separately — the point Lesson 9 confirms explicitly
It means the dashboard cannot include any calculated measures
It means the SSIS package no longer needs to load dw.FactWorkOrder
It means Power BI must use DirectQuery instead of Import
questions.explain: Reading the same warehouse tables directly is what keeps SSRS and Power BI in agreement — no divergent business logic, no separate copies to keep in sync.
